channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Turkey Mend Differences, Reaffirm "Indestructible" Solidarity
item.description: Azerbaijani leader Ilham Aliyev and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan displayed mutual admiration, dispelling rumors of tension. They met in Shusha to commemorate Azerbaijan's reconquest of Nagorno-Karabakh, glossing over recent diplomatic disputes. Both leaders emphasized their unbreakable alliance, stating their unity will endure.

item.title: China Cultural Center Planned for Opening in Astana by Year-End
item.description: Following the closing ceremony of the cross-Year of Culture between Kazakhstan and China, which featured around 40 events, plans were announced to open a Chinese Cultural Center in Astana by the end of the year. The Ministry of Culture and Information of the Republic of Kazakhstan reported this. The event included a concert and exhibition.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Gold and Foreign Exchange Reserves Hit Lowest Since December 2025
item.description: Uzbekistan's gold and foreign exchange reserves fell to $63.63 billion as of November 1, a decrease of $2.96 billion in one month, reaching the lowest point since December 2025. International reserves have declined for the second consecutive month, primarily due to a drop in gold prices on the world market.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Flights to Kazakhstan and China Following Aviation Talks
item.description: Uzbekistan has agreed with Kazakhstan and China to increase the number of flights following a civil aviation cooperation meeting in Tashkent. Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan will increase regular flights between Tashkent and Almaty/Astana from 42 to 60 weekly. Uzbekistan and China will increase flights from 100 to 114 weekly.

item.title: Russian Delegation Travels to Abu Dhabi for Trilateral Talks with US and Ukraine
item.description: A Russian delegation has departed for Abu Dhabi to participate in trilateral talks with the United States and Ukraine concerning the war in Ukraine. The meetings, scheduled for November 10-11, will focus on security guarantees, with representatives from European countries not attending.

item.title: III Uzbek-Russian Media Forum Explores New Cooperation Prospects
item.description: The III Uzbek-Russian Media Forum, held in Tashkent, brings together over 200 delegates from information sectors of both countries. Organized by Uzbekistan's National Information Agency (UzA) and Russia's TASS, the forum discusses national information space development amid technological changes. It highlights media's role in shaping public opinion and international image, and strengthening mutual understanding.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Three New Indices for National Capital Market
item.description: Uzbekistan's Republican Stock Exchange "Tashkent" will introduce three new indices: UPI, UPI FF, and UPI EW, replacing the current UCI index from November 10, 2026. This initiative aims to improve Uzbekistan's capital market position in international rankings, as per a presidential decree. The new indices will allow for stock valuation based on market capitalization, free float, and equal-weighting methods, enabling diverse analysis of the national stock market dynamics.

item.title: Elon Musk Highlights Starlink's Life-Saving Role in Kazakhstan Rescue
item.description: Elon Musk praised Starlink's success in saving lives after five individuals were stranded in a snow-covered mountainous region of East Kazakhstan. Their vehicle broke down, and they used satellite internet to contact rescuers. Musk commented on social media, stating, 'Starlink saves lives,' following the successful operation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan Boost Livestock Sector Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing international cooperation in its livestock sector to modernize operations, increase meat and dairy production, and improve breeding. Collaboration with Kazakhstan includes strengthening the feed base, livestock trade, and establishing joint breeding complexes in Belarus. Discussions focused on AI, farm cooperation, genetics, and logistics.

item.title: Uzbekistan Studies South Korean Digital Social Protection Experience
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan's National Social Protection Agency completed a two-week training course in South Korea. They studied the Korean pension system and the digitalization of social protection services. The delegation visited the 'Government 24' portal and learned about the Social Security Information Service (SSiS), which uses AI to support social workers and has reduced application processing times.

item.title: Kyrgyz Minister Visits Belarusian Industrial Enterprises, Discusses Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry, Erlist Akunbekov, visited Belarus. He toured industrial enterprises, including the "Belneftekhim" concern and the "Zhdanoichi" agro-combine. Discussions focused on exporting Belarusian products to Kyrgyzstan and exchanging experiences in vegetable and dairy processing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet Chairman to attend COP31 climate conference in Turkey
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet Chairman, Adylbek Kasymaliev, will travel to Turkey from November 10-12 for an official visit. He is scheduled to participate in the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change in Antalya. The agenda includes the opening ceremony and a high-level session on mountain ecosystems.

item.title: France blames Iran's IRGC for widespread cyberattacks on European refrigeration systems
item.description: France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of orchestrating cyberattacks that disrupted refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets across Europe. The attacks, which occurred on October 11, exploited outdated software, causing spoilage of goods and fires. France summoned the Iranian ambassador and proposed EU sanctions.

item.title: Uzbekistan represented at Beijing Forum on Civilizational Development
item.description: Uzbekistan participated in the 23rd Beijing Forum themed 'Harmony of Civilizations and Prosperity for All – Scientific and Technological Transformation and Civilizational Diversity.' The forum, organized by Peking University and other institutions, brought together over 500 scholars and experts from 30 countries to promote humanitarian sciences and intercultural dialogue.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia to Enhance Media Cooperation at Third Joint Forum
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia are set to strengthen their cooperation in the media sphere, as discussed at the third Uzbek-Russian media forum in Tashkent. Discussions focused on expanding information exchange, joint media projects, and the impact of modern technologies. TASS Director-General Andrey Kondrashov proposed developing joint TV and digital projects, while UzA Director-General Abdusaid Kuchimov emphasized media's role in intercultural dialogue and information reliability.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Retail Price of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) by 2.5 Times
item.description: Starting November 15, Uzbekistan will raise the retail price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from 2,000 UZS per kilogram to 5,000 UZS. This price hike was outlined in a government resolution dated October 31. The increase is expected to impact households significantly, raising questions about market reforms versus public affordability.

item.title: Vaccine Distrust Leaves Afghan Children Vulnerable to Preventable Diseases
item.description: Some families in Afghanistan are avoiding childhood vaccinations due to concerns about side effects and distrust of health institutions. Health experts warn that this hesitancy leaves children susceptible to preventable diseases, despite some parents believing their children are healthy without immunization.

item.title: UN Urges Tajikistan to Stop Persecuting Journalists and Opposition Figures
item.description: At a UN Human Rights Council meeting, Western countries urged Tajikistan to cease the persecution of journalists, human rights defenders, lawyers, and political opponents. They called for the release of arbitrarily detained individuals and an end to extraterritorial persecution.

item.title: Turkey: 16 Dead, 13 Injured in Blast at Izmir Metallurgy Plant
item.description: An explosion followed by a fire at the Habaş Demir-Çelik metallurgy plant in Turkey's Izmir province has resulted in 16 fatalities and 13 injuries, with two in critical condition. Search operations are ongoing for four missing individuals. The incident occurred during steel production.

item.title: Astana Police Launch Suicide Investigation in Residential Complex
item.description: Astana police have opened a criminal case following a reported suicide in a residential complex. The investigation is ongoing, and further details are not being disclosed. Reports suggest the incident may involve two teenage girls, though official information remains limited.

item.title: Tachar Province Blast Kills One, Injures Another
item.description: A homemade bomb explosion in the Khwaja Ghar district of Tachar province has resulted in one death and one injury, according to the Taliban's provincial security command. The incident occurred in the "Migrants' Mosque" area. The victims were reportedly collecting old musical instruments when the device detonated. This follows a similar incident in Ghazni province yesterday.

item.title: Russia Blocks Import of Contaminated Tomatoes from Turkmenistan
item.description: Russian agricultural inspectors intercepted four batches of fresh tomatoes, totaling 36 tons, from Turkmenistan at an Omsk warehouse. The tomatoes were found to be infected with the Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus, a dangerous quarantine object capable of destroying up to 100% of greenhouse yields. The contaminated shipment was destroyed.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine, US to Hold Peace Talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Russia, Ukraine, and the United States are set to convene for trilateral peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11. The talks aim to revive diplomatic efforts to end the ongoing conflict. Key issues are expected to include security guarantees, with European representatives not participating directly. Delegations will include high-level officials from all three nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Receives $15.2 Billion in Migrant Remittances Over Nine Months, an 8.9% Increase
item.description: Migrants sent $15.2 billion to Uzbekistan in the first nine months of the year, marking an 8.9% increase compared to the same period last year. This significant inflow of funds highlights the growing contribution of migrant labor to the Uzbek economy.

item.title: Former Afghan Police Chief Appears in Taliban Video, Alleging Planned Attacks
item.description: A video released by a Taliban-affiliated outlet shows Allah Dad Fidai, a former police chief, confessing to planning attacks against the Taliban. Fidai claims he received instructions from Sami Sadat of the Afghanistan United Front. The circumstances of the video's recording are unknown, and his claims could not be independently verified.

item.title: IOM Chief Warns Millions Face Displacement Due to Climate Inaction
item.description: The International Organization for Migration warns that insufficient climate adaptation investment is leaving vulnerable communities exposed, risking millions more displacements. Disasters caused nearly 30 million internal displacements in 2025, with storms being a major factor. The IOM urges increased long-term investment in adaptation measures.

item.title: Trump Questions Integrity of US Midterm Elections Amidst Democratic Gains
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump has questioned the health and transparency of the recent midterm elections, which saw significant gains for the Democratic Party. He expressed skepticism on social media about the fairness of the results, citing unusually large vote counts and suggesting issues with voting machines.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Sign Cooperation Agreements, Boost Bilateral Trade Prospects
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon's visit to Astana resulted in a framework agreement on petroleum product supplies and a roadmap to expand bilateral trade through 2030. Fourteen intergovernmental documents were signed, covering electricity, mining, healthcare, AI, and e-commerce, with a business forum generating $135.3 million in commercial agreements.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Tax Breaks for Educational Material Publishers
item.description: A proposed law in Uzbekistan aims to grant tax exemptions on property and land for publishers of educational materials. To qualify, at least 90% of a company's revenue must come from producing these materials. The bill has passed its third reading in the Legislative Chamber and moves to the Senate for further review.

item.title: Tashkent's Former City Hall Building Sold for 251.6 Billion Soums at Auction
item.description: The administrative building of the State Assets Management Agency in Tashkent, which previously housed the city's khokimiyat, has been sold via online auction for 251.6 billion soums. The starting price was 165.5 billion soums, with the final price increasing by 52%. The buyer, Jarkurgan Build Group, must maintain the property for office and service use.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Report Progress in Reducing Poverty
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan report progress in reducing poverty, with Uzbekistan's rate falling to 3.6% in the first nine months of 2026. Factors include job expansion, welfare increases, and formalized informal employment. Remittances also contribute significantly to poverty reduction in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Daily Digest: Key Events of November 9
item.description: A summary of key events in Kyrgyzstan on November 9 includes the full restoration of the 'Supara Chunkurchak' ethno-complex after a fire. President Sadyr Japarov explained land allocation limits for housing construction and the conditions for a 4% mortgage. Preliminary voter lists for the presidential election were published.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes 133 Projects Worth $3.3 Billion for Aral Sea Fund Presidency
item.description: Uzbekistan has prepared 133 projects totaling $3.3 billion for its presidency of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (IFAS) from 2027-2029. The projects focus on water resources, ecology, and socio-economic development, with funding sought from international financial institutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan to launch 'One Thousand Design Engineers' program with international training
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch the 'One Thousand Design Engineers' program in 2027, offering advanced training in South Korea, Japan, China, Turkey, and Europe. The initiative aims to enhance the skills of local specialists for technological development. The program will also focus on attracting highly qualified Uzbeks working abroad by providing competitive working conditions and salaries.

item.title: Kazakhstan to introduce mandatory insurance for housing against earthquakes and floods
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to implement a mandatory insurance system for residential properties covering earthquakes, floods, and forest fires. The new requirement will initially be piloted in three regions before expanding to 16 other disaster-prone areas. The initiative aims to provide financial assistance to citizens whose homes are damaged or destroyed by natural disasters.

item.title: EU Envoy Visits Tajikistan, Discusses Regional Cooperation and Energy Projects
item.description: A high-ranking European Union representative visited Dushanbe, announcing that the next EU-Central Asia meeting will be held in Tajikistan in spring 2027. Discussions focused on energy, green economy, climate change, and transport corridors. The EU plans to finance the Rogun hydropower project and supports other renewable energy initiatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Digital Family Map to Assess Family Well-being and Support Needs
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented a Digital Family Map system since 2023 to understand families' socio-economic status and identify support needs. The system, covering 6.2 million families, analyzes assets, income, and life circumstances to determine well-being levels. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection stated that asset ownership alone does not define wealth.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans $3.3 Billion in Projects During Aral Sea Fund Chairmanship
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to implement projects worth $3.3 billion during its chairmanship of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea from 2027-2029. The proposals cover water resources, ecology, and socio-economic development. Funding will come from international organizations like the World Bank and ADB. President Mirziyoyev reviewed the project presentations and approved a roadmap for next year's work.

item.title: Russian Oil Refinery Hit by Drones; Preparations for Abu Dhabi Talks
item.description: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's KINEF oil refinery in the Leningrad Oblast, with debris causing a fatality in a residential building. Russia also conducted drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian regions, causing casualties and damage to infrastructure. Meanwhile, Russia, Ukraine, and the US are set to hold talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 to cease hostilities. US President Donald Trump suggested Ukraine might look 'a little different' after the conflict.

item.title: Trump Suggests Ukraine's Territory Will Change After Conflict Ends
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated in an interview that Russia's war with Ukraine would soon end and that Ukrainian "territory" would be "a little different" afterward, without elaborating. He also believes "hate" between Zelensky and Putin hinders peace. Trump commented that Russian and Ukrainian leaders were treated "rudely" during their first meeting. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov responded that Ukrainian territory has already changed geographically, and the real situation on the ground is known.
